newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Iraq leaves bullish API report in the cold.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Iraq leaves bullish API report in the cold.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 07/18/97 WEEK ENDED 07/11/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 2.00 MLN 120,140 DN 1.249 MLN
GASOLINE........ UP 0.50 MLN 197,803 DN 2.794 MLN
UTILIZATION..... DN 0.25 PCT PT 96.7 DN 0.1 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.

Expectations for the return of Iraqi oil onto the world market dampened bullish reactions to this week's American Petroleum Institute (API) report, which showed, among other things, soaring gasoline demand.
"The report was a little bullish but the market is not reacting bullishly because we are in a bearish mode," said Thomas Blakeslee, an analyst and trader with Cargill Investor Services in New York.
The market is braced for the return of Iraqi barrels next month after the United Nation and Iraq took another step this week toward agreeing on renewal of the oil-for-food scheme.
The API report, however, may fuel a near-term upward move.
"The (price) collapse won't come tomorrow," said Pat Hughes a market analyst with Chevron Corp in Walnut Creek, California.

On ACCESS, NYMEX September crude, the new nearby contract following August crude's expiry Tuesday, was down 10 cents at $19.08 a barrel after the API report showed stocks building by 1.42 million barrels to 318.6 million barrels. But without the West Coast, that build became a draw of 1.03 million barrels.
Fueled by what some traders called record implied gasoline demand of 8.88 million barrels per day (bpd), August gasoline was up 18 points at 60.20 cents a gallon.
API said gasoline stocks fell by 2.79 million barrels to 197.8 million despite both high output and imports of 8.02 million bpd and 458,000 bpd respectively.

On the distillate side, a drop of 1.25 million barrels that brought stocks to 120.1 million laid waste to forecasts for a build of 2.0 million barrels. But August heating oil was about steady from the earlier close at 52.70 cents a gallon.
"I would gather that the (API) report would be supportive for products," Hughes said referring to the drops in gasoline and distillate stocks.

But some analysts cautioned that the draw in East Coast reformulated gasoline stocks was a disappointing one million barrels a day, and that more broadly speaking, the API implied demand may be inflating interpretations of demand at the pump.

"The high implied demand numbers for the past two weeks capture the stock shift from primary to secondary storage and that can't continue for much longer," said Richard Redash, senior energy analyst at Prudential Securities in New York.
Refinery run rates ticked down by a negligible 0.1 percentage point, leaving utilization at the still-high level of 96.7 percent.
